name: Ayta Magbukun
confidence_why: The community orthography (Komunidad ng Ayta Magbukun, DepEd Bataan & SIL 2024) marks stress with an acute on either the penult or the final syllable of look-alike words, and Cruz & Piedad 2022 likewise find stress on the final or penultimate syllable with no statable rule, but their 600-word corpus yielded no minimal pair, so the contrastive status of stress is asserted rather than demonstrated.

catalog_quote: May tatlong tuldik na maaaring gamitin ang Magbukun: pahilis ( ´), paiwa ( `), at pakupya ( ˆ). Gagamitin ito sa mga salitáng magkakahawig ang sulat subalit iba ang kahulugan. Narito ang gámit nila. (a) Ginagamit ang pahilis para markahán ang pantig na may diin. Maaari ito sa mga salitáng binibigkas nang malumay: áhu ‘áso’; dúngu ‘sikmura’; lábuk ‘buhok’; úu ‘ulo’. Ginagamit din ito para sa mga salitang binibigkas nang mabilis: buyá ‘bigas’; buktút ‘buntis’; maí ‘mais’; tuúk ‘tainga’; mangán ‘kain’. (b) Ginagamit ang paiwa para markahán ang salitáng nagtatapos sa impit na tunog na binibigkas nang malumì: kakà ‘ate/kuya’; dirà ‘mutà’; gawù ‘tuyong buho na ginagamit sa apoy’. (c) Ginagamit ang pakupya para markahán ang salitáng may impit na tunog at diin sa hulíng pantig: kalupî ‘bayong’; hirâ ‘karne/sira’. [Ayta Magbukun column, same page: Inggagamit ti hay pahili tamung markaan ti hay pantig ga main diin. Maari ti hati ha haw halitang imbibigka ung malumanay: ... Inggagamit mut bayi ti hati para ha haw halitang imbibigka ung mabili: ...]

new_statements.translation: Three diacritics may be used in Magbukun: acute ( ´ ), grave ( ` ) and circumflex ( ˆ ). They are to be used on words that are spelled alike but differ in meaning. ... (a) The acute is used to mark the syllable that carries the stress. It can be used on words pronounced malumay [penultimate stress]: áhu 'dog', dúngu 'stomach', lábuk 'hair', úu 'head'. It is also used for words pronounced mabilis [final stress]: buyá 'husked rice', buktút 'pregnant', maí 'corn', tuúk 'ear', mangán 'eat'. ... (c) The circumflex is used to mark a word that has a [final] glottal stop and stress on the last syllable: kalupî 'palm-leaf bag', hirâ 'meat / broken'.

new_statements.rule_in_words: Word stress falls on either the penultimate or the final syllable and is a lexical property of the word (Filipino-style malumay = penult vs mabilis = final classes); it is not predictable from spelling, so the orthography marks it with an acute (or, combined with a final glottal stop, a circumflex) where homographs must be distinguished. No default position is stated.
new_statements.exceptions: None; diacritics are prescribed only 'for words spelled alike but different in meaning', implying stress is otherwise left unmarked. Grave/circumflex additionally encode a word-final glottal stop (malumì = penult stress + final glottal; maragsâ-type = final stress + final glottal).
new_statements.domain_note: Orthography guide: statements concern citation forms of single words (basic vocabulary list pp. 35 ff. is printed with acute accents on many entries, e.g. abágat, abáya, kaanakán, labíng pitú, providing per-word stress data). Not an acoustic or phonological analysis; the instrumental/phonological treatment is Cruz & Piedad 2022 (not retrieved).
new_statements.identity_note: Source describes 'Ayta Magbukun' (= Bataan Ayta, Magbikin/Magbeken, Mariveleño; Glottolog bata1297, ISO 639-3 ayt), produced with the Ayta Magbukun community (Bangkal, Abucay, Bataan is named), DepEd Schools Division of Bataan and SIL Philippines; published by the Komisyon sa Wikang Filipino. Same languoid as the target; no sub-dialect specified. The 1974 Malicsi thesis on 'Halitaq Baytan (a Sambal Aeta dialect)' is probably also this language ('speech of Bataan') but that identification is unverified.

new_statements.quote: Ang stress sa wikang Ayta Magbukun ay nakikita sa paghaba at pagkakaroon ng diin sa isang tunog na patinig. Sa mga salitang mayroong dalawa hanggang tatlong pantig, malimit na nasa pinakahuli o ikalawa sa pinakahuling pantig ang diin. Sa mga salita namang mayroong higit sa tatlong pantig, hindi na madaling masabi ang posisyon ng diin. [p. 39] ... Sa mga datos na nakalap, walang salitang nakuha na nagpapatunay na phonemic o nagdudulot ng pag-iiba ng kahulugan ng salita ang haba at diin sa Ayta Magbukun. [p. 40]
new_statements.translation: Stress in the Ayta Magbukun language is seen in the lengthening of, and the placing of emphasis on, a vowel sound. In words with two to three syllables, the stress is usually on the last or the second-to-last syllable. In words with more than three syllables, the position of the stress is no longer easy to state. [p. 39] ... In the data gathered, no word was obtained that proves that length and stress are phonemic or bring about a difference in word meaning in Ayta Magbukun. [p. 40]

new_statements.relation_note: Compatible with the catalog's 'lexical (unpredictable)' reading taken from the 2024 KWF orthography (stress marked by acute/grave/circumflex on the stressed syllable of look-alike words): Cruz & Piedad likewise find stress on the final or penultimate syllable with no rule, and unpredictable in longer words. It adds the phonetic correlate (vowel length), the length/stress interaction, and a caveat: their word-list data produced no minimal pair, so they do not confirm that stress is phonemic, whereas the orthography's diacritic rule presupposes stress-distinguished homographs. The open_url itself (swfupdiliman.org) could not be reached by automated download; the full text was obtained from CO…
new_statements.rule_in_words: Stress is realized by vowel lengthening plus prominence. In 2- and 3-syllable words it falls on either the final or the penultimate syllable, word by word (Talaan 6: ˈʤaː.jaʔ 'blood' vs ha.ˈjaw 'dance'; na.ˈwiː.ni 'body' vs ma.hag.ˈmak 'many'); in words of more than three syllables no position can be stated (the four 4-syllable examples show stress on the 1st, 2nd, 3rd and 4th syllables respectively: ˈmaː.ʔa.ʤa.jɔʔ 'far', nag.ˈtuː.tu.kaʔ 'sleepy', pa.li.ˈbaː.bɔ 'upward', ha.li.pa.ˈtan 'forget'). Within the authors' ~600-word list no minimal pair was found, so they leave the phonemic status of stress and length unconfirmed ('hindi sapat ang mga nakalap na datos upang ituring na phonemic ang diin at haba', p. 43).
new_statements.exceptions: Words longer than three syllables: position 'not easy to state'. Stressed vowels are lengthened; word-final vowels may also be lengthened independently of stress (sec. 4.2.1, Larawan 4 [ˈʔaː.guː], p. 39). No consonant gemination found. Pitch, intonation and tone were not studied for lack of data (p. 39).
new_statements.identity_note: Cruz & Piedad describe Ayta Magbukun (ISO ayt) of Bataan province; data from three native-speaker consultants (Aldrin Cayetano, Vilma Cayetano, Nelia Gulisan), elicited and recorded 4 Oct 2019 with the UP Department of Linguistics 600+-item word list; the consultants' town is not named (speakers live in Abucay, Bagac, Balanga, Limay, Mariveles, Morong, Orani, Orion and Samal, p. 28). Same variety as the 2024 KWF orthography already in the catalog.

readall_conflicts: One tension, not a contradiction of placement. The catalog's existing statement (KWF/DepEd Bataan/SIL 2024 orthography, sec. 5 'Taw Tuldik') says the diacritics mark the stressed syllable in words that are spelled alike but differ in meaning, which presupposes that stress is contrastive. Cruz & Piedad 2022 (p. 40, p. 43) report that in their ~600-word list 'walang salitang nakuha na nagpapatunay na phonemic.. ang haba at diin' (no word was found proving length and stress phonemic) and explicitly call their data insufficient to decide. Both sources agree that placement is final or penultimate on a word-by-word basis with no stateable rule, so the 'lexical (unpredictable)' reading stands; the phonemic status of stress is asserted by the orthography and left open by the phonology paper.
